justification: Claim ledger rows, the claim-runner map and a pinned-set test. No served code, no data write. Not Minor: it defines the owner-approved sign-off metric. Not Critical: no query or API behaviour changes.

falsifiable_check.command: python scripts/outreach_claim_checks.py OC-30 && python -m pytest tests/test_dq_check_outreach.py -q
falsifiable_check.fails_when: The recall claim stops reading the live brief rows, or the ledger and runner disagree on the claim set OC-1..OC-30.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Seen red twice: the runner exited with a usage error for OC-23..OC-29 before they were mapped, and test_the_committed_claim_set_matches_the_decision failed with 7 extra claims until the pinned set was updated. Now OC-30 prints 156/166 = 94% and 13 tests pass.

pre_impl.existing_data: Reads live project_brief_rows (8,976 rows) and regulatory_provisions; reads nothing it does not already read.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: Main's OC-22 is the housing-reform-area claim, so the plan's recall claim cannot be OC-22; it is OC-30.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Adds 8 claim rows; existing OC-1..OC-22 untouched.

functions.name: main
functions.input: claim id from the command line, looked up in the CHECKS map (OC-23..OC-30 added)
functions.output: PASS, FAIL or UNKNOWN lines and an exit code
functions.if_none: an unknown claim id exits 2 with a usage message

functions.name: heading_read
functions.input: the recorded heading read file and the live brief rows
functions.output: PASS, FAIL or UNKNOWN with counts of flagged, house and general headings
functions.if_none: a missing or malformed file reads FAIL with a clear message, never a pass

values.value: brief rows on their cited page
values.if_missing: the check reports UNKNOWN, never a pass

break_it.scenario: A claim is declared true but its check cannot run on this machine.
break_it.what_happens: It must read UNKNOWN, not pass.
break_it.how: OC-24/26/28 printed UNKNOWN (no node_modules) and OC-27 UNKNOWN (no preview URL); none counted as a pass.

break_it.scenario: Two sessions reuse the same OC number for different claims.
break_it.how: OB-1 recall moved to OC-30; the pinned-set test lists every id.

break_it.scenario: OC-29 is declared true on a script read of the council's own section headings (34 rows, 6 named councils, 0 flagged); the check fails on a stale, malformed or incomplete record. Declared false earlier the same day when an owner read was retracted.
break_it.how: OC-29 is declared true on a script read of the council's own section headings (34 rows, 6 named councils, 0 flagged); the check fails on a stale, malformed or incomplete record. Declared false earlier the same day when an owner read was retracted.

break_it.scenario: A claim is declared true while its check cannot pass.
break_it.what_happens: CI fails with a contradicted claim.
break_it.how: OC-29 is declared true on a script read of the council's own section headings (34 rows, 6 named councils, 0 flagged); the check fails on a stale, malformed or incomplete record. Declared false earlier the same day when an owner read was retracted.

break_it.scenario: The brief is rebuilt or reloaded after the owner read.
break_it.what_happens: The recorded first clauses no longer match the rows.
break_it.how: heading_read compares every recorded first clause to the row's first clause now and returns FAIL when any differs.
break_it.repro: python scripts/outreach_claim_checks.py OC-29 after any reload of project_brief_rows

break_it.scenario: A marks file with duplicate rows or invalid marks is recorded.
break_it.what_happens: A false sign-off could read PASS.
break_it.how: heading_read requires exactly 30 distinct rows numbered 1 to 30, valid marks, at least 5 councils, and 30 distinct council-topic keys.
break_it.repro: python scripts/outreach_claim_checks.py OC-29 after duplicating a row in the data file

break_it.scenario: A flagged first rule is hidden by listing only clean councils.
break_it.what_happens: The read could pass while a named council has a wrong-type first rule.
break_it.how: The data file records how councils were named (no red first rule and recall of at least 80%) and the check fails on stale rows; the named list is fixed in the file, not chosen by the check.

post_merge.manual_verify: Run python scripts/dq_check.py --outreach with a long timeout and read which claims are not READY.
